description:
## Goal

Land one ordinary, truthful foreign boundary for Kernel/runtime operations. Fz source uses private extern "C" defp or extern "fz" defp declarations whose resolved signature is the authority. Interpreter, JIT, and AOT consume that same declaration; no source spelling, canonical type rendering, prefix, or suffix grants semantics.

The end state is one physical runtime manifest for source-visible exports, one generalized fixed-pair C result path, ordinary total C arithmetic calls, and no duplicate raw signature tables, intrinsic syntax, hidden name interception, boxed scalar transport, output pointers, arithmetic-native replacement tables, or migration debris.

## Settled contract

- Only private source extern declarations are admitted until public-FFI policy exists. extern "C" passes declared arguments; extern "fz" prepends the current process through the existing ABI.
- C scalar mapping is integer = int64_t, float = double, boolean = a word with C truthiness: 0 is false and every nonzero word is true. Fz emits canonical 0/1 boolean arguments; foreign results decode by C truthiness. Fz atom IDs are never boolean wire values.
- A C extern result may be one fixed two-field tuple over integer, float, and boolean. It is a by-value C struct adapted directly to existing Fz return lanes. No Rust tuples, generic transmutes, output pointers, or tuple boxes merely cross the boundary. Aggregate C arguments, nested/larger aggregates, arrays, unions, and packed layouts reject centrally. Opaque any and existing extern "fz" contracts retain their deliberate value-ref behavior.
- x86_64/x86_64h Linux/Darwin use natural I64/F64 pair lanes. AArch64 Linux/Darwin use F64/F64 only for float/float HFA and I64/I64 otherwise, with float bitcasts. Other triples reject before call emission.
- src/extern_contract.rs is the one physical authority for every source-visible runtime export, including panic/process exports. runtime_syms owns only compiler-private direct helpers. Do not add a bridge or preserve raw rows for fz_panic, fz_self, fz_make_ref, fz_make_resource, fz_spawn, or fz_send.

## Arithmetic

- C arithmetic exports are total. Fallible operations return {value, boolean}: checked i64 overflow returns wrapped value plus true; invalid integer div/rem returns {0, true} except MIN rem -1 which is {0, false}; failed float arithmetic returns {0.0, true}. Finite signed zeros/subnormals are valid. C never raises or carries hidden exception state.
- Kernel retains the one private generic arithmetic_result/1 source helper and arithmetic_error/0 panic endpoint. It is currently an ordinary Fz function call, not compiler magic. Its two concrete result-pair specializations and direct failure path are expected until fz-5xp.20 provides a general ordinary-call inliner. This ticket must not add a macro, duplicate every operator body, or add a special arithmetic lowering merely to hide that cost.
- This ticket deliberately does not substitute arithmetic C calls with native scalar operations. Kernel arithmetic remains an ordinary manifest-shaped C call in interpreter, JIT, and AOT. A later optimizer may recognize a higher-level resolved operator reference such as &+/2. Do not retain arithmetic binding tables, special lowering, call-elimination assertions, or temporary instrumentation here.
- Resolved, validated comparison replacement remains separate and must never use symbol spelling or rendered types as authority.

## Required proofs

1. RED-test then implement ordinary user-owned pair-return externs through interpreter, JIT, and AOT for all supported physical families, including whole tuple, destructured, and ignored-field consumers.
2. Prove malformed aggregate C arguments and runtime physical declarations reject at shared resolution before unsafe lowering.
3. Prove exact target classification and rejected untested triples.
4. Prove direct total arithmetic result/status values at overflow, division/remainder, signed-zero, finite, and nonfinite boundaries through ordinary C calls.
5. Fix the exposed canonical-type defect: equivalent result/status tuple patterns must have one canonical semantic form. Do not alter semantic source behavior or use rendered types as identity.
6. Re-measure causal facts, frontier, evaluations, body walks, and artifacts for the ordinary helper boundary. Update exact expectation only where it reports this deliberate function edge truthfully; do not add compensating scanner, bridge, private cone, or alternate metric subsystem. fz-5xp.20 owns eliminating ordinary call-boundary work.
7. Delete name intercepts, raw aliases, spawn/2 heap-hint plumbing, stale runtime imports, strict-boolean trap machinery, arithmetic substitution machinery, helper-specific workaround tests, and any compatibility path replaced by this contract.

## Acceptance

- One resolved extern contract determines source validation, interpreter call shape, JIT/AOT signature, and source-visible runtime physical ABI.
- Same source semantic answer and result/status lanes in interpreter, JIT, and AOT; ordinary C arithmetic exports remain directly callable.
- No display strings/canonical type renderings/name suffixes decide semantics.
- Full relevant fixture/CLI/AOT suites, cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test --workspace --all-features pass.
- Update .agent/docs/externs.md, .agent/docs/semantic-authorities.md, and guides/externs.html; remove temporary migration probes.

## Delivery/order

This is one ticket, one reviewed commit, one close. Keep the draft PR stacked. After source is settled and before final gates/push, rebase the complete stack from the moved fz-5xp.101/bitstring-call-carrier tip, resolve conflicts, and force-with-lease push the stack. Do not change a ready-for-review predecessor without a material rebase/change.

## UNBLOCKS

- fz-5xp.32 P2 Validate every runtime-owned extern against one exact physical ABI manifest
title: Make Kernel externs truthful and keep arithmetic total and unboxed
